hypothesis.cheapest_refuting_observation: Read the target symbol's own extent. config/GUNE5D/symbols.txt records `lbl_801160D4 = .rodata:0x801160D4; size:0xF data:string` - 15 bytes, not 16 - and the next symbol lbl_801160E8 starts 0x14 later. If the retail symbol were 0x10, the `[16]` spelling would be the faithful one and the 52-byte loss would be an objdiff pairing artifact to route around rather than a signal to obey. Measured 2026-09-03: it is 0xF, so `[16]` is the unfaithful spelling and the metric is right to reject it.
hypothesis.count_consequence: Count-neutral and word-neutral in .text throughout: MBNewNode stayed 68/68 at 23 raw differing words in every state. The entire effect of both spellings is in non-text sections.
hypothesis.screened_against_target: yes - the gap was found in `fnasm.py game/mb/mb_tree MBNewNode --raw --diff`, where target rows +0x7c/+0x84 relocate `lbl_801160D4` while ours relocated `@@595`, and the identity was confirmed by defake_gate against the target's own relocation table: target reloc[9] and reloc[10] in MBNewNode and reloc[7]/reloc[8] in MBCreateNode are all `lbl_801160D4` (0x801160D4), which our new symbol matches.
hypothesis.statement: The missing byte is TAIL PADDING after a 15-byte string, and the two things a flip needs are scored by different machinery that the extent spelling puts in tension. objdiff credits this section 52/52 at SYMBOL granularity with relocations resolved, and keeps crediting it while our raw section is one byte short; declaring the extent `[16]` makes the raw bytes and the size right (datadiff 100% at 0x34) and simultaneously breaks the symbol-granularity pairing that was earning the 432, because our symbol is then 16 bytes against the target symbol's 0xF. The untried route is therefore to supply the pad WITHOUT widening the symbol: keep `lbl_801160D4[]` unsized and add whatever retail has AFTER it in this TU's .rodata (a further data object, or a section alignment directive), so the section reaches 0x34 while the string symbol stays 15 bytes.
